Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call so we stay aligned:

- Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit in 2025. We maintain the control set and run annual external audits; we can provide a redacted SOC 2 summary under NDA (attached).
- We offer a standard DPA for GDPR and can sign a BAA for HIPAA-covered deployments (most customers doing PHI opt for Private deployment + BAA).

2) Audit logging (what we discussed) - high level

- Immutability: logs are stored in append-only storage with tamper-evident metadata; retention and WORM can be configured for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Exportability: logs can be exported on-demand to your S3 (push) or pulled via our export API; schema is JSONL - sample attached.
- Retention: default 90 days for Hosted; Dedicated/Private can configure 1+ year retention and archival policies.

Hi Alex -

Quick technical notes and sample attached (audit-logs-sample.jsonl):

- Hosted vs Dedicated immutability:
  * Hosted: default retention 90 days; logs are stored with tamper-evident checksums and internal write-once lifecycle, but external WORM enforcement (customer-controlled) is only available with Dedicated/Private deployments.
  * Dedicated/Private: configurable WORM (Write-Once Read-Many) policies, S3 object lock support, and longer retention windows (1y+).

- Export / latency:
  * Incremental exports: supported via our logs API (cursor-based).
  * Bulk exports: typical throughput allows exporting ~50GB/hour to a pushed S3 destination; smaller exports (a few GB) complete in minutes. Performance depends on chosen retention/archival tiers.

- Log schema (minimal fields we include):
  * timestamp
  * actor_id (internal user id or service principal)
  * actor_type (user/service)
  * action (e.g., "model.infer", "admin.update_policy")
  * request_id
  * model_id
  * request_tokens (count)
  * source_ip
  * response_status
  * prompt_redacted (boolean) - by default prompts are stored for 30 days in Hosted and can be redacted or excluded in Dedicated/Private.

I attached a small JSONL sample showing a few events and a short README with the logs API endpoint and example curl commands.

If you want, we can stand up a temporary export to an Acme S3 bucket during the technical session so you can ingest and validate the format live.

Thanks,
